outcome: special care nursery/neonatal intensive care unit (SCN/NICU) admission
cohort: The study included 9743 singleton births occurring during wildfire seasons from September 1, 2009, to December 31, 2015, across six cities in New South Wales, Australia.
finding: Short-term wildfire-specific PM2.5 exposure and its carbonaceous components showed positive associations with adverse perinatal outcomes, including preterm birth, stillbirth, and nonvertex presentation.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was listed as an outcome, with an adjusted hazard ratio of 1.01 (95% CI: 0.94, 1.08) for lag 0-6 days, suggesting no significant association with wildfire-specific PM2.5 exposure.
